notes: Single run per configuration (n=1): deltas are directional, not statistically reliable.

Eval-2 (meditation-home-design) passed 6/6 in BOTH configurations — its assertions are largely non-discriminating; a strong baseline model already flags brand-brief gaps and designs states. Future iterations need sharper assertions (e.g. evidence-class labels on rules, verification-boundary reporting).
The discriminating assertions were exactly the skill-specific ones: per-finding retest methods + evidence grading (eval-1), per-issue severity (eval-3) — the baseline failed those.

With-skill runs cost 2.4x tokens on eval-1 (207k vs 68k) and 2.2x on eval-3 (189k vs 84k); eval-2 was roughly equal (112k vs 109k). The overhead buys the critique contract, score bounds, and verification boundaries.
duration_ms is not exposed by the Pi subagent harness; time_seconds is 0.0 for all runs. Token counts were recovered from run inspection.
Infrastructure note: writer-subagent outputs landed in isolated git commits and had to be restored via git show; two grader subagents graded empty directories and were replaced with inline grading.
